brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Build is piece:0,0,0;half-n (Hex base · North half) — single piece, counts {piece:1}. No other bases placed.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: No neighboring bases at q±1,r±1 level 0 and no base at level 1. get_build shows only 1 node besides drawer, total parts =1 base. find_sockets for piece offered adjacent sites but none were applied.

Only one drawer per half-base cut face is allowed by configurator. find_sockets for drawer returns exactly one socket (s36: addDrawer at 0,0,0 key s). After installing one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut s:slide), further drawer adds are refused ALREADY_FITTED: 'this cut face already carries a drawer'. Notch/bay drawer frames (families notch/bay) offer 0 sockets and require two/three touching bases around an empty cell per find_sockets notes, which would violate the 'nothing beside/on top' constraint. Current build has 1 drawer, not 5 — 4 short. No configurator-allowed way to host five drawers in a single base.

finish.summary: Single half-n base built with one slide drawer (maximum allowed per single base). The 'nothing beside/on top' constraint is met. Five drawers is configurator-impossible: a half base has one cut face/one drawer slot; extra notch/bay drawers require additional adjacent bases which the brief forbids, and duplicate drawer adds are refused ALREADY_FITTED.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
